title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Tuesday afternoon, following the Presidents Day holiday on Monday.  Commissioners made quick work of a light agenda that did include a closed session.

With no visitors appearing before the council, Mayor Linda Spicer moved right into approving the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The consent agenda did include a number of items including; past meeting minutes, the warrant list, police activity report, building and zoning report and the treasurer’s report.  Also included was approval of the use of Charley Brown Park by the Bluetick Breeders and Coonhunters Association for their event April 15-18.  The body also approved Kari Thackrey’s request for Flora to host the 10th Annual 6K for Water on Saturday, May 16, with participants required to comply with local laws concerning the use of city streets.  The last item included in the consent agenda was Flora Elementary School’s use of Charley Brown Park for the Accelerated Reader Program on May 19 with a rain date of May 20.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer asked commissioners to accept the resignation of Chris Thopmson from the Flora Tourism Committee, effective February 4 with Spicer and other commissioners thanking Thompson for her years of service to Flora.

Commissioner Phil Wiley presented a proposal to purchase a budgeted item.  Wiley asked the city to purchase a Terex Hi-Ranger Optima HR55 Bucket Truck, to replace a unit that they can no longer get parts for repair.  The cost is $310,468 and the motion was approved unanimously.

City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford presented two items for the council’s consideration.  First was approval to apply for an EV Charger Grant and then an HVAC Grant for the Flora Public Library.  Both measures were approved without dissent are offered by IMEA.  Stanford also said that he heard from Matt Johnson about moving forward with the Wastewater Treatment Plant proposal.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles spoke briefly and reminds the public that applications are still needed for the summer positions of Pool Manager, Assistant Pool Manager and Lifeguards.  Please apply by February 20.

Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart presented three items for council approval.  First, was approval of Change Order #3 (Final) for Sanitary Sewer Improvements, Section 2 to Visu-Sewer of Missouri, LLC, an increase of $14,253.  Next awas approval of Payment #2 (Final) for Sanitary Sewer Improvements, Section 2 to Visu-Sewer of Missouri LLC in the amount of $17,737 and finally was Payment #1 for Unknown Lead Service Lines to Ecowash, LLC, in the amount of $31,868.  All three items were approved unanimously.

Mayor Spicer called for the council to go into closed session, with no action expected when they returned to the open meeting.

title: TAKE BACK ILLINOIS TOUR
full_story:
Gubernatorial candidate Darren Bailey, and his running mate Aaron Del Mar, are scheduling stops in the area starting tomorrow.

The candidates will appear at the Poderosa Steakhouse in Vandalia from 9 to 10 am.  Then at the Milk House in Greenville from Noon to 1 pm.  From there they move to Salem where they will appear at the Freedom Church from 3 to 4 pm.  They end Thursday with an appearance at Skateland in Fairfield from 6 to 7 pm.  On Friday the tour makes appearances at the Lumberyard in West Salem from 9 to 10 am, and at Steve Jones Hardware in Salem from 3 to 4 pm.

The duo is in the middle of a seven-day, 25-stop bus tour.  Admission to the events is free and refreshments will be available at most of the stops.

title: MASSAGE THERAPY CLINICALS
full_story:
Olney Central College’s Massage Therapy Program is accepting appointments for Spring clinicals.

The clinics are open to the public and will be held from 9:15 am to 2 pm this Saturday and also on March 20th, April 11th and April 24th at the West Richland Center in Noble.

The cost for a relaxing massage is $45 for an hour and $30 for half an hour.  A 20-minute chair massage is $20.

Clinics are by appointment only and can be made by calling 618-392-2430.  Callers should leave a message with their names, contact information and date desired.  Students will return phone messages during Monday and Wednesday evening classes to confirm appointments.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for January during Tuesday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated 11 traffic accidents.

They made 7 criminal arrests.  There were no drug or DUI arrests during January.  There was 1 local ordinance arrests, 10 traffic arrests and 2 warrant arrests.

Officers issued 38 warning tickets, responded to 22 alarms and had 1,019 calls for service and had 2 juvenile contacts.

Also, Flora police officers drove 4,971miles and conducted 42 investigations during January.  They answered 274, 911 calls and conducted 12 UTV Inspections and no Golf Cart Inspections during January.

title: FMH HIRING
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital is seeking a qualified candidate for the full-time position of Director of Plant Operations to lead and oversee facility management in support of the hospital’s mission to deliver high-quality healthcare to the community.

The Director of Plant Operations is a senior leadership role responsible for ensuring the safety, functionality, and efficiency of the hospital’s physical environment.  This position oversees all aspects of facility management, including engineering, maintenance, groundskeeping, safety, and security.  As the hospital’s Safety Officer, the Director will ensure compliance with regulatory standards and best practices while collaborating with hospital leadership to plan and execute capital projects, manage budgets, and promote continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate will have seven to ten years of supervisory experience in plant operations, maintenance, or facilities management, as well as a working knowledge of building systems, safety regulations, and preventive maintenance best practices.  A bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or a related field is preferred.

This full-time position offers a competitive salary range of $75,000 to $125,000, along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, vision and disability insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, flexible scheduling, and professional development opportunities.

Fairfield Memorial Hospital is an Equal Opportunity Employer dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.  Interested candidates are encouraged to apply online at www.fairfieldmemorial.org/careers/open-positions or contact Human Resources at 618-847-8270 for more information.

title: MEASLES DIAGNOSED
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) confirmed the state’s first measles case of 2026 in an adult from the Metro East area.  This person had recently traveled out of state.

Health officials are tracing possible exposure sites, including Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Collinsville.  Attendees there on February 8th from 8:00 am to 12:15 pm might have been exposed.

Dr. Sameer Vohra from IDPH stressed the importance of vaccination, noting, “This first reported case of measles in Illinois in 2026 is a reminder to our Illinois residents that this disease can be prevented with up-to-date vaccination.”

The MMR vaccine is 97% effective with two doses.  IDPH advises those exposed and not fully vaccinated to watch for symptoms like rash and fever.  Contact your healthcare provider before visiting if symptoms appear.

Travelers should check their vaccination status if heading to outbreak areas.  Use IDPH’s vaccine locator tool to find nearby vaccination sites.  Health providers should report suspected cases to local health departments.
